title.zh: 卷420 列傳二百七 韩超 田兴恕 曾璧光 席宝田
title.en: Volume 420 Biographies 207: Han Chao, Tian Xingshu, Ceng Biguang, Xi Baotian
title.raw: 卷420 列傳二百七 韩超 田兴恕 曾璧光 席宝田

sentences.zh: 韓超，字南溪，直隸昌黎人。

translations.literal: Han Chao, styled Nanxi, was a native of Changli in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chao, whose courtesy name was Nanxi, came from Changli in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 道光十四年，副貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of the Daoguang reign, he became a secondary tribute graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1834 he qualified as a secondary tribute graduate.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，天津治海防，超詣軍門獻策，事平，獎敘州判。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when Tianjin was organizing coastal defense, Chao went to the military headquarters to offer strategies; when the affair was settled, he was rewarded with an acting appointment as prefectural judge.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842, while Tianjin was building up its coastal defenses, Chao presented plans at army headquarters; after the crisis passed he received a commendation and an acting post as prefectural judge.

sentences.zh: 尋以府經歷揀發貴州，歷署三角屯州同、獨山知州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was selected as a prefectural clerk and sent to Guizhou, successively acting as subprefect of Sanjiaotun and magistrate of Dushan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon selected as a prefectural clerk and dispatched to Guizhou, where he served in turn as acting subprefect of Sanjiaotun and magistrate of Dushan.

sentences.zh: 獨山多盜，號難治。

translations.literal: Dushan had many bandits and was known as difficult to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Dushan was rife with bandits and had a reputation as a hard district to govern.

sentences.zh: 超募勇訓練，用土民為鄉導，擒其渠。

translations.literal: Chao recruited braves and trained them, using local people as guides, and captured their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Chao raised and drilled a militia, employed locals as guides, and seized the bandit chiefs.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼守黎平，深倚重之，言之巡撫蔣霨遠，超由是知名。

translations.literal: When Hu Linyi was defending Liping he relied on Chao heavily, spoke of him to the governor Jiang Yuanyuan, and Chao became well known from this.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi, then holding Liping, came to depend on him deeply and recommended him to Governor Jiang Yuanyuan, and Chao's name spread from that time.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，烏沙苗倡亂，超從林翼進剿，馳風雪中，先後斬獲數百人，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, the Miao of Wusha rose in rebellion; Chao followed Linyi in the punitive campaign, riding through wind and snow, and in succession killed or captured several hundred men until the remnant bands were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 the Wusha Miao rebelled; Chao marched with Linyi to suppress them, fighting through blizzards until he had killed or captured hundreds and the last rebels were subdued.

sentences.zh: 論功，以知縣用。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, he was recommended for use as a county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was nominated for appointment as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 二年，署清江通判。

translations.literal: In the second year he acted as subprefect of Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as acting subprefect of Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 知黔將亂，捐俸豢勇士八十人，練成勁卒。

translations.literal: Knowing that Guizhou was about to fall into disorder, he donated his salary to maintain eighty brave men and trained them into a crack force.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing turmoil in Guizhou, he spent his own salary to keep eighty fighting men and drilled them into a hardened corps.

sentences.zh: 四年，獨山土匪結粵匪內犯，超率兵練迎擊，分軍出賊後，攻其不備，擒賊首楊元保，复深入廣西南丹州境，擊諸匪平之，加同知銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, bandits of Dushan joined with Guangdong rebels in an invasion from within; Chao led troops and militia to meet them, divided his forces to strike behind the enemy and attack where they were unprepared, captured the bandit chief Yang Yuanbao, again advanced deep into Nanzhou in Guangxi, struck the various bandits and pacified them, was given the rank of subprefect, and was awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 local bandits in Dushan allied with Cantonese rebels in a joint assault; Chao led regulars and militia to meet them, sent a detachment around the enemy rear for a surprise attack, captured the chief Yang Yuanbao, then pushed into Nanzhou prefecture in Guangxi and cleared the bandits there, earning an acting subprefect's rank and the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 桐梓匪楊鳳竄永寧，合黔西匪王三扎巴連陷數城，圍遵義，超馳至，敗賊南關，陣斬王三扎巴，立解城圍。

translations.literal: The Tongzi bandit Yang Feng fled to Yongning and joined with the Qianxi bandit Wang Sanzhaba in seizing several cities in succession and besieging Zunyi; Chao rushed there, defeated the bandits at the South Gate, slew Wang Sanzhaba in battle, and immediately lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng of Tongzi fled to Yongning and, with the Qianxi rebel Wang Sanzhaba, took several towns and encircled Zunyi; Chao hurried up, routed the enemy at the south gate, killed Wang Sanzhaba on the field, and relieved the city at once.

sentences.zh: 复追敗諸葛章司河，擒楊鳳斬之，餘黨盡殲，擢知府。

translations.literal: Again he pursued and defeated them at Zhugezhang Sihe, captured Yang Feng and executed him, and the remnant bands were annihilated; he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them again at Zhugezhang Sihe, took Yang Feng and beheaded him, and wiped out the survivors, for which he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 五年，苗亂蔓延，超馳援台拱，解黃平、平越圍；

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Miao rebellion spread; Chao hurried to aid Taigong and relieved the sieges of Huangping and Pingyue;
translations.idiomatic: In 1855, as the Miao revolt widened, he rushed to Taigong and broke the sieges of Huangping and Pingyue;

sentences.zh: 轉戰至施秉、鎮遠，賊塹山斷道，以阻官軍。

translations.literal: fighting on to Shibing and Zhenyuan, the bandits entrenched on the mountains and cut the roads to block the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: he fought on toward Shibing and Zhenyuan, where the rebels had dug in on the heights and severed the roads to stop the imperial columns.

sentences.zh: 超以孤軍馳突其間，大小數十戰，補石阡知府。

translations.literal: Chao with a lone army dashed among them through several dozen battles large and small, and was appointed prefect of Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Chao drove a solitary column through their lines in dozens of engagements and was appointed prefect of Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 超性剛直，有膽略，每與上官爭執是非，上官責以勦賊而靳其餉，飢師轉戰，往往求協助於鄰省。

translations.literal: Chao's nature was upright and firm, with courage and resource; he often disputed right and wrong with his superiors, and superiors charged him with suppressing bandits while withholding his pay, so that hungry troops fought on campaign and he often had to seek aid from neighboring provinces.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was blunt and principled, bold and resourceful; he frequently argued policy with his superiors, who ordered him to fight rebels while stinting his supplies, so his half-starved men campaigned on and he often had to beg help from neighboring provinces.

sentences.zh: 四川總督駱秉章、湖北巡撫胡林翼交章論薦，侍郎王茂廕亦疏薦之，詔下巡撫問狀，以道員記名。

translations.literal: Sichuan Governor Luo Bingzhang and Hubei Governor Hu Linyi jointly memorialized recommending him, Vice Minister Wang Maoyin also memorialized recommending him, an edict was sent down to the governor to inquire into his conduct, and he was placed on the list for appointment as a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Luo Bingzhang of Sichuan and Hu Linyi of Hubei both filed joint recommendations, Vice Minister Wang Maoyin also recommended him, the throne ordered the provincial governor to report on his record, and he was registered for promotion to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 九年，授貴州糧儲道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Grain Intendant of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he was made Grain Intendant of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 時苗、教各匪連陷諸郡縣，駐軍卭水汛，扼其中，使苗、教不得合，且遏其下竄湖南之路。

translations.literal: At that time Miao and sectarian bandits had in succession seized many prefectures and counties; he stationed troops at the Qingshui garrison, held the center so that Miao and sectarians could not unite, and also blocked their route of descent into Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Miao and religious rebels had by then overrun one district after another; he held the Qingshui post in the middle to keep the two rebel streams apart and to choke off their path south into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 賊出全力撲之，超約楚軍夾擊，賊大潰。

translations.literal: The bandits threw their full strength against him; Chao arranged with the Hunan army for a pincer attack and the bandits were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hurled their full force at him; Chao coordinated a converging strike with Hunan troops and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 剿思州響鼓坪，施秉土地坪，鎮遠金鼎𡉫、鋒嚴𡉫、唐家營𡉫諸賊巢，擒賊目張東山、歐光義等，鎮遠所屬皆平。

translations.literal: He suppressed the bandit nests at Xiangguping in Sizhou, Tudiping in Shibing, and Jindingzhai, Fengyanzhai, and Tangjiayingzhai in Zhenyuan, captured the bandit leaders Zhang Dongshan and Ou Guangyi and others, and all districts under Zhenyuan were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed rebel strongholds at Xiangguping in Sizhou, Tudiping in Shibing, and the Jinding, Fengyan, and Tangjiaying stockades in Zhenyuan, took chiefs such as Zhang Dongshan and Ou Guangyi, and brought the whole Zhenyuan region under control.

sentences.zh: 民團舊以十戶養一壯丁，超因其意稍變通之，官募士而民輸糧；

translations.literal: The old militia system had ten households maintain one able-bodied man; Chao following its intent made a slight modification, with the government recruiting soldiers while the people supplied grain;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old militia rule ten households supported one fighting man; Chao adapted the idea so that the state enlisted troops while civilians paid grain;

sentences.zh: 又籍叛產分授降眾、流人，以田代餉；

translations.literal: he also registered rebel property and distributed it to surrendered masses and displaced persons, using land in place of pay;
translations.idiomatic: he also parceled out confiscated rebel land to surrendered rebels and refugees in lieu of rations;

sentences.zh: 行之二年，得兵三千人。

translations.literal: after two years of this he had three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: and within two years had raised three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 自軍興，協餉不至，地方官吏爭抽取釐金以為補助。

translations.literal: Since the armies had been raised, cooperative funds had not arrived, and local officials competed to levy likin as a supplement.
translations.idiomatic: After the war began, cooperative subsidies never came, and local officials vied to levy likin transit taxes to make up the gap.

sentences.zh: 超建議釐金統一，一抽之後，不復再抽，商無滯累，餉用差給。

translations.literal: Chao proposed unifying the likin levy so that after one collection there would be no second, merchants would not be burdened with delays, and funds would be somewhat supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Chao urged a single standardized likin rate—one levy only, no repeat exactions—so trade would flow and pay would be roughly met.

sentences.zh: 十年，命幫辦貴州剿匪事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to assist in Guizhou bandit suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he was assigned to help direct the Guizhou pacification.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he acted as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he served as acting provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 提督田興恕疏陳超前後戰功，加布政使銜，賜號武勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Provincial Military Commissioner Tian Xingshu memorialized Chao's successive battle merits; he was given the rank of provincial treasurer and awarded the title Brave Martial Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commander Tian Xingshu reported Chao's campaigns in detail; he received the rank of provincial treasurer and the title Brave Martial Batulu.

sentences.zh: 詔予二品頂戴，​​署貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: An edict granted him a second-rank official's cap button and appointed him acting governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him a second-rank cap button and made him acting governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 田興恕方以欽差大臣督辦軍務，超久在行間，亦以肅清全黔為己任。

translations.literal: Tian Xingshu was then Imperial Commissioner supervising military affairs; Chao had long been in the field and also took the pacification of all Guizhou as his own duty.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xingshu was then Imperial Commissioner in charge of operations; Chao, who had spent years in the field, likewise made clearing the whole province his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，田興恕罷，乃命超辦理防剿事宜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Tian Xingshu was dismissed, and Chao was then ordered to handle defense and suppression affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, when Tian Xingshu was removed, Chao was put in charge of defense and pacification.

sentences.zh: 時尚大坪、玉華山兩處為賊巢，遵義、安順、思南、大定、銅仁、石阡諸府所在皆賊，五月，回匪陷興義，雲南叛回潰勇擾境，粵匪亦由川竄至正陽、廟堂並桐梓、松坎諸地。

translations.literal: At that time Shangdaping and Yuhuashan were two bandit nests; Zunyi, Anshun, Sinan, Dading, Tongren, and Shiqian and other prefectures were everywhere infested with bandits; in the fifth month the Hui rebels seized Xingyi, Yunnan mutinous Hui stragglers disturbed the borders, and Guangdong bandits also from Sichuan raided Zhengyang, Miaotang, and Tongzi and Songkan and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel bases still held Shangdaping and Yuhuashan; bandits overran Zunyi, Anshun, Sinan, Dading, Tongren, Shiqian, and neighboring prefectures; in the fifth month Hui rebels took Xingyi, fugitive Yunnan Hui troops raided the frontier, and Cantonese rebels slipped in from Sichuan toward Zhengyang, Miaotang, Tongzi, Songkan, and the like.

sentences.zh: 超令總兵吳安康進剿，用內應夜縱火攻破賊巢，擒匪首倪老帽斬之，出難民二千餘人。

translations.literal: Chao ordered Brigadier Wu Ankang to advance in suppression; using an inside agent they set fire by night and broke the bandit nest, captured the bandit chief Ni Laomao and executed him, and released more than two thousand refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent Brigadier Wu Ankang against them; with inside help the troops fired the camp at night, stormed the lair, seized the chief Ni Laomao and executed him, and freed more than two thousand civilians.

sentences.zh: 六月，閔家場踞賊糾集苗、教諸黨偪江口，天柱匪首亦糾合土匪攻陷縣城，分股竄湖南晃州廳、高寨，陷卭水、青谿兩城，謀截楚軍糧道。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, bandits occupying Minjiachang gathered Miao and sectarian factions to press on Jiangkou; the Tianzhu bandit chief also rallied local bandits, seized the county seat, split into columns that raided Huangzhou subprefecture and Gaozhai in Hunan, and seized the two cities of Qingshui and Qingxi, plotting to cut the Hunan army's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month rebels at Minjiachang mustered Miao and religious allies against Jiangkou; a Tianzhu chief joined hill bandits to storm the county town, sent columns into Hunan's Huangzhou and Gaozhai, took Qingshui and Qingxi, and tried to sever the Hunan army's grain route.

sentences.zh: 超令總兵羅孝連、道員趙國澍進攻安順仲匪，夷其壘，擒斬賊酋韋登鳳等。

translations.literal: Chao ordered Brigadier Luo Xiaolian and Circuit Intendant Zhao Guoshu to attack the Zhong bandits of Anshun, leveled their stockades, and captured and executed the bandit chiefs including Wei Dengfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent Brigadier Luo Xiaolian and Circuit Intendant Zhao Guoshu against the Zhong rebels of Anshun, razed their forts, and captured and beheaded chiefs such as Wei Dengfeng.

sentences.zh: 尚大坪賊复約苗、教分掠江內，超令孝連斷其歸路，國澍等馳軍迎擊，復令副將趙德元出冷水河、梯子岩進襲尚大坪，立破之，卬水汛城同時克復。

translations.literal: The Shangdaping bandits again joined Miao and sectarians to plunder within the river region; Chao ordered Xiaolian to cut their line of retreat while Guoshu and others rushed troops to meet them, and again ordered Vice Brigadier Zhao Deyuan to advance from Lengshuihe and Tiziyan to strike Shangdaping, which was immediately broken, and the Qingshui garrison city was recovered at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdaping rebels again allied with Miao and sectarians to loot the inner river districts; Chao had Xiaolian block their retreat while Guoshu met them head-on and Zhao Deyuan struck from Lengshuihe and Tiziyan; Shangdaping fell at once and the Qingshui post was retaken the same day.

sentences.zh: 進平玉華山賊巢，攻拔瓦寨，复天柱縣城，特詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Advancing to pacify the Yuhuashan bandit nest, he stormed Wazhai and recovered the Tianzhu county seat; a special edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to crush the Yuhuashan nest, took Wazhai, and restored Tianzhu county—a deed singled out for imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 道員鄧爾巽、總兵李有恆，破王家苗寨、夾馬洞諸賊巢，獲其酋李玉榮等。

translations.literal: Circuit Intendant Deng Erxun and Brigadier Li Youheng broke the bandit nests of Wangjia Miao stockade and Jiamadong and others, and captured their chiefs including Li Yurong.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Intendant Deng Erxun and Brigadier Li Youheng overran the Wangjia Miao and Jiamadong strongholds and took chiefs such as Li Yurong.

sentences.zh: 黃、白號，教匪竄遵義，知府李德莪擊破之於三台山，奪五里坎諸隘口。

translations.literal: The Yellow and White Sect religious bandits fled into Zunyi; Prefect Li De'e defeated them at Santaishan and seized the passes at Wulikan and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow- and White-Sect rebels broke into Zunyi; Prefect Li De'e routed them on Santaishan and recaptured the Wulikan passes.

sentences.zh: 副將周宏順進攻石阡，毀老王𡉫賊巢，諸𡉫就撫。

translations.literal: Vice Brigadier Zhou Hongshun advanced on Shiqian, destroyed the Laowangzhai bandit nest, and the various stockades submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Brigadier Zhou Hongshun marched on Shiqian, burned the Laowangzhai nest, and one stockade after another surrendered.

sentences.zh: 石阡、銅仁苗匪攻毀鎮遠營壘，卭水戍軍亦潰，遂南掠松桃，北攻天柱。

translations.literal: Miao bandits of Shiqian and Tongren attacked and destroyed the Zhenyuan garrison works, the Qingshui garrison troops also collapsed, and they then raided south into Songtao and attacked north toward Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Miao rebels in Shiqian and Tongren smashed the Zhenyuan camps, the Qingshui garrison broke, and the enemy swept south into Songtao and north against Tianzhu.

sentences.zh: 湖南援師至，賊始引去。

translations.literal: When Hunan relief troops arrived, the bandits only then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Hunan reinforcements came did the rebels pull back.

sentences.zh: 詔斥超專恃援軍，有負疆寄。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Chao for relying exclusively on relief troops and failing his frontier charge.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked Chao for depending too much on outside aid and neglecting his frontier mandate.

sentences.zh: 雲南方議撫回，巡撫徐之銘諮會停剿，而回匪益恣，竄陷安南、興義，分擾郎岱、永寧、歸化，詔原其誤信撫議，免議處。

translations.literal: Yunnan was then debating pacification of the Hui; Governor Xu Zhiming consulted and agreed to halt suppression, but the Hui rebels grew more insolent, raided and seized Annan and Xingyi, and separately harassed Langdai, Yongning, and Guihua; an edict excused his mistaken trust in the pacification plan and exempted him from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan was debating a conciliatory policy toward the Hui; Governor Xu Zhiming agreed to suspend fighting, yet the Hui grew bolder, seized Annan and Xingyi, and raided Langdai, Yongning, and Guihua; the court forgave Chao's misplaced faith in negotiation and dropped the charges.

sentences.zh: 石達開自川回竄，分三路，一走遵義，一走黔西，一走桐梓。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai fled back from Sichuan in three columns, one going to Zunyi, one to Qianxi, and one to Tongzi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai doubled back from Sichuan in three columns toward Zunyi, Qianxi, and Tongzi.

sentences.zh: 遣沈宏富、李有恆、余祖凱擊之。

translations.literal: Chao dispatched Shen Hongfu, Li Youheng, and Yu Zukai to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent Shen Hongfu, Li Youheng, and Yu Zukai to meet them.

sentences.zh: 田興恕以教案獲譴去官，黔軍益單。

translations.literal: Tian Xingshu was punished and removed from office over the missionary case, and the Guizhou army grew still thinner.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xingshu was disgraced and dismissed over the missionary affair, leaving the Guizhou forces still more understrength.

sentences.zh: 二年，乞病回籍。

translations.literal: In the second year he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，卒於家，年七十有九。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died at home, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in 1878, in his seventy-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 詔念前功，賜卹，諡果靖。

translations.literal: An edict recalled his former merits, granted funeral honors, and gave the posthumous title Guojing.
translations.idiomatic: The court remembered his service, granted mourning honors, and posthumously titled him Guojing.

sentences.zh: 貴州請建專祠，並附祀胡林翼祠。

translations.literal: Guizhou requested a dedicated shrine for him and also enshrined him in Hu Linyi's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou petitioned for a shrine in his honor and for his tablet to be placed in Hu Linyi's temple as well.

sentences.zh: 田興恕，字忠普，湖南鎮筸人。

translations.literal: Tian Xingshu, styled Zhongpu, was a native of Zhenjiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xingshu, courtesy name Zhongpu, was from Zhenjiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 年十六，充行伍，隸鎮筸鎮標。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he entered the ranks as a soldier and was attached to the Zhenjiang garrison battalion.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he joined the army under the Zhenjiang garrison standard.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，從守長沙。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he followed in the defense of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he took part in the defense of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 賊屯湘江西岸，軍中募敢死士夜驚賊營，興恕請行，夜浮小舟往，潛燔賊營，賊騎數百追之，泅水免。

translations.literal: The rebels were encamped on the west bank of the Xiang River; the army recruited daredevils to harass the rebel camp by night; Xingshu volunteered, at night floated a small boat over, secretly set fire to the rebel camp, several hundred rebel horsemen pursued him, and he swam away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held the west bank of the Xiang; the garrison sought volunteers for a night raid, and Xingshu went alone in a skiff, burned the enemy camp, outswam hundreds of pursuers, and got away.

sentences.zh: 巡撫駱秉章奇之，委充哨官。

translations.literal: Governor Luo Bingzhang was struck by this and appointed him a platoon officer.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Luo Bingzhang was impressed and made him a platoon officer.

sentences.zh: 五年，從克郴州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed in the capture of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he helped take Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，領五百人號虎威營。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he led five hundred men called the Tiger Might Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he commanded five hundred men in the Tiger Might Battalion.

sentences.zh: 從蕭啟江援江西，克萬載、袁州。

translations.literal: He followed Xiao Qijiang to relieve Jiangxi and captured Wanzai and Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Xiao Qijiang to relieve Jiangxi and captured Wanzai and Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，戰上高英岡嶺，深入被圍，左手受創，亡馬，步戰，他將馳救，得免。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he fought at Shanggao Yinggangling, advanced deep and was surrounded, was wounded in the left hand, lost his horse, fought on foot, and another general rushed to rescue him and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 at Shanggao Yinggangling he pushed too far, was surrounded, took a wound in the left hand, lost his horse, fought on foot until another officer rode in and pulled him out.

sentences.zh: 是役以少擊眾，斃賊千數。

translations.literal: In this battle with few he struck many and killed bandits by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In that fight his small force killed rebels by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 進攻臨江，掘地道轟城，先登，再被創，賊死拒未下。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Linjiang, they dug a tunnel to bombard the wall, he was first to scale, was wounded again, and the rebels resisted to the death and the city was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: At Linjiang his men mined the walls; he led the escalade, was wounded again, and the defenders held so fiercely that the city still did not fall.

sentences.zh: 援賊大至，啟江議暫退，興恕不可，曰：「兵在精不在多，原為前鋒。

translations.literal: Relief bandits arrived in great force; Qijiang proposed a temporary withdrawal, but Xingshu would not agree, saying: "Troops depend on quality not numbers; I was meant to be the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy reinforcements poured in; Qijiang urged a pullback, but Xingshu refused, saying, "Soldiers win by skill, not numbers—I am here to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 」率所部直貫賊陣，賊張左右翼圍之，後軍望見興恕旗指東麾西，賊皆披靡，夾擊，賊大敗竄走，遂復臨江。

translations.literal: "He led his unit straight through the bandit formation; the bandits spread left and right wings to surround him; the rear army saw Xingshu's banner pointing east and commanding west, the bandits all scattered, they struck from both sides, the bandits were utterly defeated and fled, and Linjiang was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " He drove his men straight through the rebel line; when the enemy tried to envelop him, the rear columns saw his banner wheel east and west, the rebels broke, a converging attack crushed them, and Linjiang was retaken.

sentences.zh: 八年，克崇仁、樂安、宜黃、南豐，積功至副將，加總兵銜，賜號尚勇、摯勇兩巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he captured Chongren, Le'an, Yihuang, and Nanfeng; for accumulated merit he reached vice brigadier, was given the rank of brigadier, and was awarded the titles Shangyong and Zhiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he took Chongren, Le'an, Yihuang, and Nanfeng, rose to vice brigadier and then brigadier, and received the titles Valiant and Steadfast Batulu.

sentences.zh: 貴州苗、教匪熾，黎平府被圍久。

translations.literal: Guizhou Miao and sectarian bandits were fierce and Liping prefecture had long been besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Miao and sectarian rebels raged in Guizhou, and Liping had been under siege for a long time.

sentences.zh: 興恕奉檄赴援，至即攻破賊營，連戰三日而圍解，進克古州、永從，署古州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Xingshu received orders to go to the relief; on arrival he immediately broke the bandit camps, fought three days in succession and the siege was lifted, advanced to capture Guzhou and Yongcong, and acted as commander of Guzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to the rescue, he smashed the rebel camps as soon as he arrived, fought three days straight to lift the siege, then took Guzhou and Yongcong and served as commander of the Guzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開圍寶慶，興恕率四千五百人赴援，扼九鞏橋，無日不戰，歷月餘，糧藥將罄，選死士欲以一戰決勝負，會李續宜援軍至，內外夾擊，毀附城營三，連日攻下，勢如破竹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Dakai besieged Baoxing; Xingshu led four thousand five hundred men to the relief, held Jiugong Bridge, and fought every day for more than a month; grain and munitions were nearly exhausted and he selected daredevils intending to settle the issue in one battle; then Li Xuyi's relief army arrived, they struck from inside and outside, destroyed three camps adjoining the city, and in successive days stormed and took them with irresistible force.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 Shi Dakai besieged Baoxing; Xingshu brought forty-five hundred men to Jiugong Bridge and fought daily for over a month until supplies ran low; he picked shock troops for a decisive battle just as Li Xuyi's reinforcements came, and together they tore down three camps by the walls and swept the rest away.

sentences.zh: 達開竄廣西，遂移軍靖州防黔邊，命署貴州提督，督辦貴州軍務，增軍盈二萬。

translations.literal: Dakai fled to Guangxi, and he then moved the army to Jingzhou to guard the Guizhou border; he was ordered to act as Guizhou provincial military commissioner, to supervise Guizhou military affairs, and his army increased to more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai fled into Guangxi; Xingshu shifted to Jingzhou to watch the Guizhou frontier, was made acting provincial commander, took charge of Guizhou operations, and expanded his force past twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 十年，道銅仁，取印江，分軍略思南、石阡，進克貓貓山賊巢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year on the road through Tongren he took Yinjiang, divided his army to overrun Sinan and Shiqian, and advanced to capture the Maomaoshan bandit nest.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, marching through Tongren, he seized Yinjiang, sent columns through Sinan and Shiqian, and stormed the Maomaoshan rebel nest.

sentences.zh: 石達開由廣西入貴州，連陷數縣，省城大震。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai entered Guizhou from Guangxi, seized several counties in succession, and the provincial capital was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai entered Guizhou from Guangxi, took county after county, and panic spread in the capital.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉源灝趣赴援，興恕奏言：「黔省上游道路分歧，賊若以一軍擾黔，一軍入蜀，道遠兵單，斷難兼顧。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Yuanhao urged him to hurry to the relief; Xingshu memorialized saying: "In the upper reaches of Guizhou the roads branch in many directions; if the bandits send one army to harass Guizhou and one army into Sichuan, the roads are long and troops few and it will be hard to attend to both.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Yuanhao pressed him to hurry; Xingshu replied that upstream Guizhou's roads forked everywhere—if rebels tied down Guizhou while another column entered Sichuan, distance and thin numbers would make both fronts impossible.

sentences.zh: 已檄韓超防鎮遠，沈宏富守湄潭，劉義方進松桃，臣駐石阡，居中調度。

translations.literal: I have already ordered Han Chao to defend Zhenyuan, Shen Hongfu to hold Meitan, Liu Yifang to advance on Songtao, and I myself will station at Shiqian to direct from the center.
translations.idiomatic: He had already posted Han Chao at Zhenyuan, Shen Hongfu at Meitan, and Liu Yifang toward Songtao, while he himself held Shiqian to coordinate.

sentences.zh: 賊如上竄，則親會川軍以攻之；

translations.literal: If the bandits move upstream, I will personally join Sichuan troops to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: If they moved upriver he would join Sichuan forces in person;

sentences.zh: 窺楚，即馳還靖州。

translations.literal: if they watch Chu, I will hurry back to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: if they threatened Hunan he would ride back to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」時興恕已實授提督，詔授欽差大臣，命援省城。

translations.literal: "At that time Xingshu had already been confirmed as provincial commander; an edict appointed him Imperial Commissioner and ordered him to relieve the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had been confirmed as provincial commander; the court named him Imperial Commissioner and ordered him to save the capital.

sentences.zh: 師至，部署省防，督軍赴定番迎剿，賊棄城而走。

translations.literal: When the army arrived he deployed provincial defenses, supervised troops to meet and suppress at Dingfan, and the bandits abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he organized the capital's defenses, led troops out to Dingfan, and the rebels abandoned the city and ran.

sentences.zh: 十一年，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he also acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he also served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 時回、仲、苗、教諸匪分擾，上下游幾無完土。

translations.literal: At that time Hui, Zhong, Miao, and sectarian bandits harassed in separate groups, and upstream and downstream there was almost no intact territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, Zhong, Miao, and sectarian rebels then harried the province in every quarter until scarcely a district was untouched.

sentences.zh: 興恕分兵援剿，戰屢捷。

translations.literal: Xingshu divided troops to aid in suppression and won repeated victories in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshu split his forces for joint campaigns and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 招撫匪首唐天佑、賈福保、陳大六、柳天成等，克復歸化、荔波、定番、廣順、獨山諸城，疏通驛路，軍威漸振。

translations.literal: He recruited and pacified the bandit chiefs Tang Tianyou, Jia Fubao, Chen Daliu, Liu Tiancheng and others, recovered Guihua, Libo, Dingfan, Guangshun, Dushan and other cities, cleared the courier routes, and military prestige gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: He induced chiefs such as Tang Tianyou, Jia Fubao, Chen Daliu, and Liu Tiancheng to submit, retook Guihua, Libo, Dingfan, Guangshun, Dushan, and other towns, reopened the post roads, and slowly restored the army's standing.

sentences.zh: 興恕年甫二十有四，驟膺疆寄，恃功而驕，又不諳文法，左右用事，屢被論劾，乃罷兼職，以韓超代之。

translations.literal: Xingshu was only twenty-four years old and suddenly bore a frontier charge; relying on his merits he grew proud, and not understanding civil law, his close associates wielded power; he was repeatedly impeached, was then removed from the concurrent post, and Han Chao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Only twenty-four, he had suddenly been given a frontier command; flush with success he turned arrogant, ignorant of civil procedure, and let favorites rule for him until repeated impeachments cost him the governorship, which Han Chao took over.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，罷欽差大臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was dismissed as Imperial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he lost the Imperial Commissionership.

sentences.zh: 會法國教士文乃爾傳教入黔，因事齟齬，興恕惡其倔強，殺之，坐褫職，赴四川聽候查辦。

translations.literal: When the French missionary Wén Nai'er came to Guizhou to preach and friction arose over an incident, Xingshu detested his obstinacy and killed him; he was punished by removal from office and sent to Sichuan to await investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When the French missionary Wén Nai'er entered Guizhou and a dispute turned ugly, Xingshu, angered by his defiance, had him killed; he was stripped of office and ordered to Sichuan to await trial.

sentences.zh: 經遵義旺超，值雲貴總督勞崇光為賊所困。

translations.literal: Passing Wangchao in Zunyi, he encountered Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Lao Chongguang beset by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On the road through Zunyi at Wangchao he found Governor-General Lao Chongguang trapped by rebels.

sentences.zh: 興恕驟馬衝入，大呼：「田某在此！

translations.literal: Xingshu suddenly charged in on horseback and shouted loudly: "Tian is here!
translations.idiomatic: Xingshu spurred straight in and shouted, "Tian is here!

sentences.zh: 」賊驚潰，翼崇光出。

translations.literal: "The bandits fled in alarm, and he escorted Chongguang out.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels scattered in panic and he escorted Lao out.

sentences.zh: 尋論罪遣戍新疆，行至甘肅，總督左宗棠奏請留防秦州。

translations.literal: Soon he was sentenced and sent into exile in Xinjiang; reaching Gansu, Governor-General Zuo Zongtang memorialized asking that he be kept to defend Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon condemned to exile in Xinjiang; in Gansu, Governor-General Zuo Zongtang pleaded to keep him for defense at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，釋歸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 he was pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in 1877.

sentences.zh: 曾璧光，字樞垣，四川洪雅人。

translations.literal: Ceng Biguang, styled Shuyuan, was a native of Hongya in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Biguang, courtesy name Shuyuan, was from Hongya in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，記名御史。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler and placed on the list for censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he earned his jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, became a compiler, and was marked for appointment as a censor.

sentences.zh: 入直上書房，授恭親王奕訢、醇郡王奕枻讀。

translations.literal: He entered the Upper Study Hall and instructed Prince Yixin the Prince Gong and Prince Yixuan the Prince Chun in reading.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Upper Study Hall and tutored Prince Gong Yixin and Prince Chun Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年，出為貴州鎮遠知府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he went out as prefect of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he left the capital to serve as prefect of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，署貴東道。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he acted as Guizhou East Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he acted as intendant of Guizhou East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二年，剿平銅仁踞賊蕭文魁，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the second year he suppressed the bandits entrenched at Tongren led by Xiao Wenkui and was awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he crushed the Tongren rebels under Xiao Wenkui and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 雲貴總督勞崇光薦其才，迭署糧道、按察使、布政使。

translations.literal: Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Lao Chongguang recommended his talent; he was successively appointed acting grain intendant, judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lao Chongguang praised his ability, and he served in turn as acting grain intendant, judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 六年，予二品頂戴，​​署貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given a second-rank cap button and appointed acting governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he received a second-rank cap button and was made acting governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，實授。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was confirmed in the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his appointment was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 貴州地瘠亂久，北境接四川，東境接湖南，軍事悉倚鄰援，​​本省餉既艱窘，將多驕蹇。

translations.literal: Guizhou's land was poor and disorder had lasted long; its northern border adjoined Sichuan and its eastern border adjoined Hunan; military affairs all depended on neighboring aid, and the province's own funds were already strained while many generals were proud and insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou was poor soil and had been at war for years; its north touched Sichuan and its east Hunan, so every campaign leaned on neighbors, while provincial pay was exhausted and many commanders were arrogant and unruly.

sentences.zh: 總兵林自清劾罷後，戕興義縣令，率所部萬人擾川境。

translations.literal: After Brigadier Lin Ziqing was impeached and dismissed, he killed the magistrate of Xingyi and led his ten thousand men to harass the Sichuan border.
translations.idiomatic: After Brigadier Lin Ziqing was cashiered, he murdered the Xingyi magistrate and led ten thousand men to raid the Sichuan frontier.

sentences.zh: 八年，璧光密遣提督陳希祥擒斬之，令吳宗蘭剿青山餘匪，克普安、安南。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Biguang secretly sent Provincial Commander Chen Xixiang to capture and execute him, ordered Wu Zonglan to suppress the remnant bandits at Qingshan, and captured Pu'an and Annan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 Biguang secretly sent Provincial Commander Chen Xixiang to seize and behead Lin, had Wu Zonglan clear the Qingshan remnants, and recovered Pu'an and Annan.

sentences.zh: 時席寶田軍已由東路進規台拱，省城附近諸匪糅雜，出沒無常。

translations.literal: At that time Xi Baotian's army had already advanced from the east toward Taigong, while the various bandits near the provincial capital were mixed together and appeared and vanished without pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Baotian was already pushing east toward Taigong, while mixed rebel bands around the capital raided without pattern.

sentences.zh: 九年，周達武調任貴州提督，率川軍至貴陽，漸次勘定。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Zhou Dawu was transferred to be Guizhou provincial commander, led Sichuan troops to Guiyang, and gradually pacified the province.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 Zhou Dawu became Guizhou commander, brought Sichuan troops to Guiyang, and step by step brought order.

sentences.zh: 自軍興鄉試久停，至是年始補行，人心益定。

translations.literal: Since the armies had been raised the provincial examinations had long been suspended; in this year they were at last held as a supplement, and popular sentiment grew still more settled.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial exams had been suspended since the war; they were finally held again that year, and public morale steadied further.

sentences.zh: 與達武議增兵扼要駐守，令道員蹇訚破遵義賊，擒其酋吳三；

translations.literal: He discussed with Dawu increasing troops to hold key points in garrison, ordered Circuit Intendant Jian Yin to break the Zunyi bandits and capture their chief Wu San;
translations.idiomatic: With Dawu he agreed to reinforce key posts, sent Circuit Intendant Jian Yin against the Zunyi rebels, and took their chief Wu San;

sentences.zh: 令提督劉士奇克都勻，殪其酋吳章。

translations.literal: and ordered Provincial Commander Liu Shiji to capture Duyun and destroy its chief Wu Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Provincial Commander Liu Shiji to take Duyun and kill its chief Wu Zhang.

sentences.zh: 十年，令提督鍾有思等進剿上游，克永寧、威寧，下游諸軍擒悍賊潘得洪，收復八寨等城。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he ordered Provincial Commander Zhong Yousi and others to advance in suppression upriver, captured Yongning and Weining, and downstream the various armies captured the fierce bandit Pan Dehong and recovered Bazhai and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he sent Zhong Yousi upriver to take Yongning and Weining, while downstream columns seized the fierce Pan Dehong and retook Bazhai and neighboring towns.

sentences.zh: 又收復上江、下江、三腳各城，平上游鎮寧、歸化賊巢，殪永城踞賊侯大五，斬郎岱金家硐踞賊金大七，盤江北岸肅清。

translations.literal: Again he recovered the cities of Shangjiang, Xiajiang, and Sanjiao, pacified the bandit nests of Zhenning and Guihua upriver, destroyed the entrenched bandit Hou Dawu of Yongcheng, beheaded the entrenched bandit Jin Daqi of Jinjiadong in Langdai, and the north bank of the Pan River was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He also retook Shangjiang, Xiajiang, and Sanjiao, cleared rebel nests at Zhenning and Guihua, killed the Yongcheng chief Hou Dawu and the Langdai strongman Jin Daqi, and swept the north bank of the Pan.

sentences.zh: 又破畢節、威寧諸匪，清八寨、三角餘賊，毀其巢。

translations.literal: Again he broke the bandits of Bijie and Weining, cleared the remnant bandits of Bazhai and Sanjiao, and destroyed their nests.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed the Bijie and Weining rebels, mopped up Bazhai and Sanjiao survivors, and burned their lairs.

sentences.zh: 令總兵何世華擊斬安南賊酋潘么，進克貞豐，西路悉平。

translations.literal: He ordered Brigadier He Shihua to strike and kill the Annan bandit chief Pan Yao, advanced to capture Zhenfeng, and the western route was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Brigadier He Shihua killed the Annan chief Pan Yao, took Zhenfeng, and the whole western front was quiet.

sentences.zh: 十一年，周達武率所部會楚軍定苗疆，詔嘉調度有方，予優敘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Zhou Dawu led his troops to join the Hunan army in settling the Miao frontier; an edict praised his skillful direction and granted him preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 Zhou Dawu and Hunan allies finished the Miao frontier; the court praised his coordination and gave him preferential honors.

sentences.zh: 十二年，會滇軍克新城老巢，全省肅清，加太子少保、頭品頂戴，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he joined Yunnan troops in capturing the old nest at Xincheng; the whole province was pacified; he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and a first-rank cap button and awarded the hereditary yunqiwei rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 Yunnan troops helped take the Xincheng nest, the province was declared clear, and Biguang received Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, a first-rank button, and a hereditary yunqiwei rank.

sentences.zh: 尋新城防軍索餉譁變，匪首何玉亭攻新城，遣其黨黎正關攻興義，分軍馳剿，捕誅其渠，事旋定。

translations.literal: Soon the Xincheng garrison mutinied demanding pay; the bandit chief He Yuting attacked Xincheng and sent his follower Li Zhengguan to attack Xingyi; troops were divided to rush in suppression, the ringleaders were captured and executed, and the affair was soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Xincheng garrison mutinied for pay; chief He Yuting stormed Xincheng while Li Zhengguan hit Xingyi; columns rushed to suppress them, the leaders were taken and killed, and order returned.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，卒於官，追贈太子太保，依總督例賜卹，諡文誠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he died in office; posthumously he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, funeral honors according to the governor precedent, and the posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 1875; the court posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted governor-level mourning honors, and titled him Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 四川、貴州請建專祠。

translations.literal: Sichuan and Guizhou requested dedicated shrines for him.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan and Guizhou petitioned for shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 席寶田，字研薌，湖南東安人。

translations.literal: Xi Baotian, styled Yanxiang, was a native of Dong'an in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Baotian, courtesy name Yanxiang, came from Dong'an in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the licentiate degree.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，率鄉團殺賊，复縣城，獎敘訓導。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he led the local militia to kill bandits and recover the county seat, and was rewarded with an acting appointment as director of studies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he led local militia against bandits, retook the county seat, and earned an acting post as director of studies.

sentences.zh: 六年，劉長佑援江西，招參軍事，遂從轉戰，積功累擢同知直隸州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Liu Changyou went to relieve Jiangxi and recruited him to military affairs; he then followed in the campaigns and for accumulated merit was repeatedly promoted to subprefect of Zhili prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 Liu Changyou marched to Jiangxi, took him on staff, and through successive campaigns he rose to subprefect of a Zhili prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開由廣西犯湖南，寶田從解寶慶圍，擢知府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Dakai from Guangxi invaded Hunan; Baotian followed in relieving the siege of Baoxing and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, when Shi Dakai invaded Hunan from Guangxi, Baotian helped lift the siege of Baoxing and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 十年，駱秉章令募千人號精毅營，防湖南邊。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Luo Bingzhang ordered him to recruit a thousand men called the Elite Steadfast Battalion to guard the Hunan border.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Luo Bingzhang had him raise a thousand-man Elite Steadfast Battalion for the Hunan frontier.

sentences.zh: 廣東賊犯郴州、桂陽，擊走之。

translations.literal: Guangdong bandits invaded Chenzhou and Guiyang and he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Cantonese rebels struck Chenzhou and Guiyang, he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，石達開復由廣西入境，連敗之於黔陽，克來鳳，以道員記名，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Shi Dakai again entered from Guangxi; he defeated him repeatedly at Qianyang, captured Laifeng, was placed on the list for circuit intendant, and was given the rank of provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 Shi Dakai again came from Guangxi; Baotian routed him at Qianyang, took Laifeng, was marked for circuit intendant, and received the rank of provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，粵匪黃文金大舉犯江西，命提督江忠義赴援，寶田副之，戰饒州桃溪渡，大破之；

translations.literal: In the second year the Guangdong bandit Huang Wenjin invaded Jiangxi in force; Provincial Commander Jiang Zhongyi was ordered to the relief and Baotian served as his deputy; they fought at Raozhou Taoxi Ford and inflicted a great defeat;
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 Huang Wenjin's Cantonese rebels swept into Jiangxi; Jiang Zhongyi was sent to meet them with Baotian as deputy; at Raozhou Taoxi Ford they won a crushing victory;

sentences.zh: 又迭破之於湖口、洋塘、石門、青山橋，賊引去，趨池州，圍青陽。

translations.literal: again and again they defeated him at Hukou, Yangtang, Shimen, and Qingshan Bridge; the bandits withdrew and moved toward Chizhou and besieged Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: then beat him again at Hukou, Yangtang, Shimen, and Qingshan Bridge until the rebels withdrew toward Chizhou and besieged Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 寶田襲石嶺，破賊卡，分軍遮其前，命水陸夾擊，文金遁走，遂解青陽圍，累功賜號業鏗額巴圖魯，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Baotian raided Shiling, broke the bandit stockade, divided his army to block their front, ordered joint land and water attack, Wenjin fled, and the siege of Qingyang was lifted; for accumulated merit he was awarded the title Yekenge Batulu and given the rank of provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Baotian stormed Shiling, smashed the rebel post, blocked their front, ordered a combined land-and-water strike, and Wenjin fled; Qingyang was relieved, and he earned the title Yekenge Batulu and provincial treasurer's rank.

sentences.zh: 江忠義卒於軍，寶田代領其眾，留防江西。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyi died in the army and Baotian took command of his forces and remained to defend Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Zhongyi died in camp, Baotian took over his troops and stayed to hold Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 三年，李世賢、黃文金復合犯江西，將以遙掣江寧之師，寶田逆擊白沙關，奪梘橋要隘，鈔擊於大濟關、泥嶺關，賊竄山谷，復金谿，以按察使記名，授雲南按察使。

translations.literal: In the third year Li Shixian and Huang Wenjin again combined to invade Jiangxi intending to tie down the Nanjing army from afar; Baotian met them at Baishaguan, seized the Ji Bridge pass, struck at Dajiguan and Niliguan, the bandits fled into the mountains, and Jinx was recovered; he was placed on the list for provincial judicial commissioner and appointed judicial commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Li Shixian and Huang Wenjin again joined to raid Jiangxi and threaten Nanjing from afar; Baotian met them at Baishaguan, took Ji Bridge pass, ambushed them at Dajiguan and Niliguan, drove them into the hills, retook Jinx, was marked for provincial judicial commissioner, and was appointed to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時楊岳斌初至江西督辦軍務，檄寶田援南豐，坐遷延被劾，降知府，留軍。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Yuebin had just arrived in Jiangxi to supervise military affairs and ordered Baotian to relieve Nanfeng; for delay he was impeached, reduced to prefect, and kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuebin had just arrived to direct Jiangxi operations and ordered Baotian to Nanfeng; impeached for delay, he was demoted to prefect but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 會大軍克江寧，群賊擁洪秀全子福瑱逸出，由開化犯玉山，走瀘溪，寶田邀擊於新城，進至石城楊家牌，擒洪仁玕、洪仁政、黃文英等。

translations.literal: When the great army captured Nanjing, the bandits escorted Hong Xiuquan's son Fuzhen in flight; they invaded Yushan from Kaihua and went to Luxi; Baotian intercepted them at Xincheng and advanced to Yangjiapai in Shicheng, capturing Hong Rengan, Hong Renzheng, Huang Wenying and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell, rebels escorted Hong Xiuquan's son Fuzhen out through Kaihua into Yushan and on to Luxi; Baotian caught them at Xincheng and at Shicheng Yangjiapai took Hong Rengan, Hong Renzheng, Huang Wenying, and others.

sentences.zh: 福瑱匿山谷中，捕得之，檻送南昌，伏誅。

translations.literal: Fuzhen hid in the mountains, was captured, sent in a cage to Nanchang, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhen was found hiding in the hills, caged to Nanchang, and executed.

sentences.zh: 詔复寶田原官，予雲騎尉世職，賜黃馬褂，授貴州按察使。

translations.literal: An edict restored Baotian to his former office, granted him the hereditary yunqiwei rank, awarded the yellow riding jacket, and appointed him Guizhou provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored his former rank, gave him a hereditary yunqiwei, the yellow riding jacket, and the Guizhou judicial commissionership.

sentences.zh: 時餘賊汪海洋等走廣東，四年，寶田自平遠邀擊，降萬餘人，又扼鐵石嶺，降者二萬，諸軍合擊於嘉應州，全數蕩平。

translations.literal: At that time the remnant bandits Wang Haiyang and others fled to Guangdong; in the fourth year Baotian from Pingyuan intercepted and attacked, and more than ten thousand surrendered; again he held Tieshiling and twenty thousand surrendered; the various armies jointly attacked at Jiaying prefecture and all were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Remnants such as Wang Haiyang fled to Guangdong; in 1865 Baotian from Pingyuan cut them off and accepted more than ten thousand surrenders, then at Tieshiling took twenty thousand more until a joint strike at Jiaying wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 論功，江西軍以寶田為第一，詔以布政使記名，遇缺題奏。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, the Jiangxi army ranked Baotian first; an edict placed him on the list for provincial treasurer to be memorialized when a vacancy arose.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi ranked him first in merit; the throne marked him for provincial treasurer at the next vacancy.

sentences.zh: 軍事既定，請回籍終養，允之。

translations.literal: When military affairs were settled he requested to return home to fulfill mourning for his mother and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the fighting ended he asked to go home and mourn his mother, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 貴州苗、教諸匪構亂十有餘年，東路素倚湖南援軍，自粵匪平後，議大舉剿平。

translations.literal: Guizhou Miao and sectarian bandits had stirred disorder for more than ten years; the eastern route had long relied on Hunan relief troops; after the Guangdong bandits were pacified, a major campaign to suppress and pacify was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Miao and religious rebels had troubled Guizhou for more than a decade, the east depending on Hunan aid; once the Cantonese rebels were gone, the court planned a full pacification.

sentences.zh: 先是授兆琛為貴州布政使，偕總兵周洪印率師往，積歲無功。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhao Chen had been appointed Guizhou provincial treasurer and together with Brigadier Zhou Hongyin led troops there, but after years achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chen had earlier been sent as provincial treasurer with Brigadier Zhou Hongyin, but years passed without success.

sentences.zh: 李元度圍荊竹園，亦久不下。

translations.literal: Li Yuandu besieged Jingzhuyuan and also could not take it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuandu besieged Jingzhuyuan just as long without result.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李瀚章、劉昆先後劾罷兆琛、洪印，元度亦鐫級，薦起寶田招集舊部萬人入貴州，總統東路諸軍。

translations.literal: Governors Li Hanzhang and Liu Kun in succession impeached and dismissed Zhao Chen and Hongyin, Yuandu was also demoted, and Baotian was recommended and raised to gather his old troops of ten thousand and enter Guizhou, commanding all eastern-route armies.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Li Hanzhang and Liu Kun cashiered Zhao Chen and Hongyin, demoted Yuandu, and brought Baotian back to lead ten thousand veterans into Guizhou as commander of the eastern front.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，進軍石阡，荊竹園為教匪老巢，寶田審視地勢高峻，匪砦環列，惟北面平夷可掩入。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year he advanced on Shiqian; Jingzhuyuan was the old nest of the sectarian bandits; Baotian surveyed the terrain as lofty and steep, with bandit stockades ranged around, and only the northern side level enough to mask an entry.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he marched on Shiqian; Jingzhuyuan was the sectarians' main nest on steep ground ringed with forts, with only the northern slope low enough for a surprise approach.

sentences.zh: 七年元旦，進攻，部將黃元果先登，諸將肉薄壘下，一日平十八砦，克荊竹園，擒斬匪首蕭桂盛、何瑞堂，其旁三十六砦相繼攻下。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the seventh year he attacked; his subordinate Huang Yuanguo was first to scale, the generals fought hand to hand below the ramparts, in one day eighteen stockades were pacified, Jingzhuyuan was taken, the bandit chiefs Xiao Guisheng and He Ruitang were captured and executed, and the thirty-six neighboring stockades were taken in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day 1868 he attacked; Huang Yuanguo led the escalade, officers fought at the walls, eighteen forts fell in a day, Jingzhuyuan was taken, chiefs Xiao Guisheng and He Ruitang were captured and killed, and thirty-six neighboring forts followed.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，被珍賚。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported he received imperial rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Victory brought imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 夏，進規寨頭。

translations.literal: In summer he advanced toward Zhaotou.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he turned toward Zhaotou.

sentences.zh: 寨頭為苗疆門戶，諸苗帑賄資糧所萃，連拔東西三屯，陣斬苗酋桂金保，破援賊張臭迷，攻下台笠、丁耙塘諸砦，遂克寨頭。

translations.literal: Zhaotou was the gateway to the Miao frontier, where the various Miao collected tribute and supplies; he took the eastern and western Santun in succession, slew the Miao chief Gui Jinbao in battle, broke the relief bandit Zhang Choumi, stormed Taizhai, Dingbatang and other stockades, and then captured Zhaotou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaotou guarded the Miao frontier and held their tribute stores; he took the eastern and western Santun, killed chief Gui Jinbao in battle, routed Zhang Choumi's relief column, stormed Taizhai and Dingbatang, and seized Zhaotou.

sentences.zh: 分軍克天柱，斬其酋陳大六。

translations.literal: He divided his army to capture Tianzhu and beheaded its chief Chen Daliu.
translations.idiomatic: A detachment took Tianzhu and beheaded its chief Chen Daliu.

sentences.zh: 會丁繼母憂，回籍治喪，提督榮維善暫領其眾，尋詔奪情趣赴​​軍，進攻台拱。

translations.literal: When his stepmother died he returned home to observe mourning; Provincial Commander Rong Weishan temporarily commanded his troops; soon an edict cut short the mourning and ordered him to the army to advance on Taigong.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died he went home to mourn; Rong Weishan held his command until an edict cut mourning short and sent him against Taigong.

sentences.zh: 台拱苗最強，踞清江、鎮遠二城為犄角。

translations.literal: The Taigong Miao were the strongest, holding Qingjiang and Zhenyuan cities as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: The Taigong Miao were the strongest, using Qingjiang and Zhenyuan as paired strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 寶田請增兵萬人，按察使黃潤昌、道員鄧子垣領之出晃州為北路，寶田自當南路，令榮維善用雕剿法，轉戰山谷間，破諸苗砦，漸近鎮遠。

translations.literal: Baotian requested ten thousand more troops; Provincial Judicial Commissioner Huang Runchang and Circuit Intendant Deng Ziyuan led them out from Huangzhou as the northern route while Baotian himself took the southern route, ordering Rong Weishan to use the "eagle pursuit" method, fighting through the mountain valleys, breaking the various Miao stockades, and gradually approaching Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Baotian asked for ten thousand reinforcements; Huang Runchang and Deng Ziyuan led the northern column from Huangzhou while he took the south and had Rong Weishan harry Miao forts through the valleys toward Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 潤昌、子垣由思州進攻鎮遠府城，克之。

translations.literal: Runchang and Ziyuan advanced from Sizhou to attack Zhenyuan prefectural city and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Runchang and Ziyuan marched from Sizhou and took Zhenyuan city.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，維善連破董敖、公鵝兩隘，遂克清江廳城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year Weishan in succession broke the Dong'ao and Gong'e passes and then captured Qingjiang subprefecture city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1869 Weishan broke the Dong'ao and Gong'e passes and took Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 兩軍合趨黃飄，山地狹峻，人行頂趾相接，遇伏。

translations.literal: The two armies converged on Huangpiao; the mountain land was narrow and steep, men marched with head and heel touching; they met an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Both columns pushed toward Huangpiao on trails so narrow men marched toe to heel—and walked into an ambush.

sentences.zh: 維善軍疾行先出險，潤昌軍誤以為陷伏中，爭道相擠，為賊所乘，潤昌、子垣皆戰歿。

translations.literal: Weishan's army marched fast and was first out of danger; Runchang's army mistakenly thought they were trapped in ambush and scrambled for the road, were seized upon by the bandits, and Runchang and Ziyuan both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Weishan's men sprinted clear first; Runchang's troops thought themselves trapped, jammed the path, and were cut down—Runchang and Ziyuan both fell.

sentences.zh: 維善聞變，率二百人馳救，被圍，為苗所擒，遇害。

translations.literal: Weishan heard of the disaster and led two hundred men to the rescue, was surrounded, was captured by the Miao, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Weishan heard, rushed two hundred men to help, was surrounded, captured by the Miao, and killed.

sentences.zh: 於是苗氛复熾。

translations.literal: Thereupon Miao unrest flared again.
translations.idiomatic: Miao resistance flared anew.

sentences.zh: 張秀眉犯巴冶，寶田親督軍擊走之，進克稿米，令龔繼昌、蘇元春破苗寨，擊走張臭迷等，分軍守鎮遠、施秉。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiumei invaded Baye; Baotian personally supervised the army to drive him off, advanced to capture Gaomi, ordered Gong Jichang and Su Yuanchun to break Miao stockades, drove off Zhang Choumi and others, and divided troops to hold Zhenyuan and Shibing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiumei struck Baye; Baotian led the counterattack, took Gaomi, had Gong Jichang and Su Yuanchun storm Miao forts, routed Zhang Choumi, and garrisoned Zhenyuan and Shibing.

sentences.zh: 時以寶田軍苦戰年餘，尚未深入，議罷其軍，劉昆仍主專任，復增兵萬人，分三路進。

translations.literal: At that time because Baotian's army had fought bitterly for more than a year and had not yet penetrated deep, there was discussion of disbanding his army; Liu Kun still advocated sole responsibility, again increased troops by ten thousand, and divided advance in three routes.
translations.idiomatic: After a year of hard fighting without deep penetration, some urged disbanding his force; Liu Kun kept him in sole command, added ten thousand men, and opened three routes.

sentences.zh: 九年，會攻施洞，克之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year they jointly attacked Shidong and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 they jointly stormed and took Shidong.

sentences.zh: 苗走九股河，白洗苗來援，擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Miao fled to Jiugu River; the Baixi Miao came to aid and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao fled to Jiugu River; Baixi Miao reinforcements were beaten off.

sentences.zh: 進攻台拱，破革夷諸砦，薄台拱城下，苗棄城走，克之，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Taigong, they broke the Geyi stockades, pressed under Taigong city walls, the Miao abandoned the city and fled, and it was captured; he was given a first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on Taigong they stormed the Geyi forts, reached the walls, the Miao abandoned the city, Taigong fell, and Baotian received a first-rank button.

sentences.zh: 進軍九股河，分別剿撫，凡平黑苗砦二百餘所。

translations.literal: Advancing on Jiugu River, they separately suppressed and pacified, and in all more than two hundred Black Miao stockades were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiugu River they alternately fought and accepted surrender until more than two hundred Black Miao forts were cleared.

sentences.zh: 雞講、丹江苗皆請歸化。

translations.literal: The Jijiang and Danjiang Miao all requested to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Jijiang and Danjiang Miao all came in.

sentences.zh: 十年，進攻凱里，一鼓而下。

translations.literal: In the tenth year they advanced to attack Kaili and took it in one assault.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 they took Kaili at the first rush.

sentences.zh: 苗潰走雷公山，麕眾六七萬人，黃茅嶺、雷口坪、九眼塘、燕子窩諸寨皆絕險，寶田督諸軍冒暑入山，合擊張臭迷，斬馘三萬，燔其廬舍，剿洗一空。

translations.literal: The Miao collapsed and fled to Leigong Mountain, gathering a crowd of sixty or seventy thousand; Huangmaoling, Leikouping, Jiuyantang, Yanziwu and other stockades were all extremely perilous; Baotian supervised the various armies entering the mountains in the heat, jointly struck Zhang Choumi, killed and captured thirty thousand, burned their dwellings, and swept the area clean.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao broke toward Leigong Mountain with sixty or seventy thousand in the fastnesses of Huangmaoling, Leikouping, Jiuyantang, and Yanziwu; Baotian led columns into the summer heat, crushed Zhang Choumi, killed or captured thirty thousand, burned their villages, and scoured the range bare.

sentences.zh: 駐軍施洞口，寶田遽病風痺，乞假醫療，命部將龔繼昌、蘇元春、唐本有、謝蘭階分統其軍。

translations.literal: Stationed at Shidongkou, Baotian suddenly fell ill with wind paralysis, begged leave for medical treatment, and ordered his subordinates Gong Jichang, Su Yuanchun, Tang Benyou, and Xie Lanjie to command his armies separately.
translations.idiomatic: Camped at Shidongkou he was struck by paralytic stroke, took medical leave, and left Gong Jichang, Su Yuanchun, Tang Benyou, and Xie Lanjie to command his divisions.

sentences.zh: 軍事進止機宜，仍禀命於寶田。

translations.literal: For military advance and halt and strategic decisions, they still reported to Baotian for orders.
translations.idiomatic: They still reported every move to Baotian for approval.

sentences.zh: 十一年，三路進兵，凱北以北悉定。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the three routes advanced; north of Kaibei was entirely settled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 the three columns advanced and secured everything north of Kaibei.

sentences.zh: 合攻烏雅坡，諸酋皆在，以長圍困之。

translations.literal: They jointly attacked Wuyapo; all the chiefs were present and were encircled with a long siege.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuyapo they besieged the chiefs together in a long encirclement.

sentences.zh: 迭戰，斬九大白、岩大五於陣，先後降者數万。

translations.literal: Fighting in succession, they slew Jiubai and Yan Dawu in battle, and those who surrendered in succession numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Battle after battle killed Jiubai and Yan Dawu on the field; tens of thousands surrendered in waves.

sentences.zh: 四月，擒張秀眉、楊大六、金大五等，檻送長沙，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they captured Zhang Xiumei, Yang Daliu, Jin Dawu and others, sent them in cages to Changsha, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they took Zhang Xiumei, Yang Daliu, Jin Dawu, and others, caged them to Changsha, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 張臭迷先逸，捕得戮之。

translations.literal: Zhang Choumi had fled earlier, was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Choumi, who had escaped earlier, was caught and put to death.

sentences.zh: 諸酋或降或斬，無脫者。

translations.literal: The various chiefs either surrendered or were executed, and none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Every chief either submitted or was killed; none escaped.

sentences.zh: 苗疆平，詔晉寶田騎都尉世職，家居養疴。

translations.literal: The Miao frontier was pacified; an edict promoted Baotian's hereditary cavalry commandant rank, and he dwelt at home nursing his illness.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao frontier was settled; the court raised his hereditary cavalry commandant rank and he retired home to convalesce.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年，詔以寶田前擒洪福瑱功，命曾國荃繪其像以進。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu an edict, because of Baotian's former merit in capturing Hong Fuzhen, ordered Zeng Guoquan to paint his portrait and present it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886, honoring his capture of Hong Fuzhen, the court had Zeng Guoquan paint his portrait for presentation.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒，贈太子少保，優恤。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died; posthumously he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and preferential mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1889, posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with special mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 原籍及江西、貴州建專祠。

translations.literal: Dedicated shrines were built in his native place and in Jiangxi and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines were raised in his home county, Jiangxi, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 論曰：貴州之匪，總名有六：曰苗匪、教匪，曰黃號、白號，其小者曰槓匪、仲匪，其他濫練、游勇、逆回、悍夷，揭竿踵起，不可悉數。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The bandits of Guizhou in general have six names: Miao bandits and sectarian bandits, Yellow Sect and White Sect, and the lesser ones called gang bandits and Zhong bandits; besides these, mutinous militia, roaming braves, rebellious Hui, and fierce barbarians raised banners in succession and cannot all be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Guizhou rebels fell under six broad heads—Miao and religious sectarians, Yellow and White Sects, plus lesser gang and Zhong bands—while mutinous militia, drifters, Hui rebels, and fierce tribesmen rose in such numbers they cannot all be listed.

sentences.zh: 始於咸豐四年，無兵無餉，不能制也。

translations.literal: Beginning in the fourth year of Xianfeng, with no troops and no funds, they could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: From 1854 onward the province lacked troops and money and could not contain them.

sentences.zh: 韓超有辦賊之才，久屈下僚，事權不屬。

translations.literal: Han Chao had the talent to handle bandits but long remained in subordinate posts without authority belonging to him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chao had real talent for suppression yet long remained a subordinate without full command.

sentences.zh: 田興恕入黔，兵威始振，超亦驟起，未久相繼去。

translations.literal: When Tian Xingshu entered Guizhou, military prestige first revived, and Chao also rose abruptly, but before long they left in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Xingshu entered Guizhou the army's standing revived and Chao rose with him, yet both soon departed.

sentences.zh: 張亮基治黔數年，亦僅補苴。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangji governed Guizhou for several years and also only patched things up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liangji governed Guizhou for years and achieved little more than stopgaps.

sentences.zh: 中原大定，曾國籓乃議以湖南兵力、餉力為平黔根本，而駱秉章亦令劉岳昭剿黔北以保川邊。

translations.literal: When the central plains were largely settled, Zeng Guofan then proposed that Hunan's military strength and fiscal strength be the foundation for pacifying Guizhou, and Luo Bingzhang also ordered Liu Yuezhao to suppress northern Guizhou to secure the Sichuan border.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heartland was calm, Zeng Guofan made Hunan's troops and treasury the basis for pacifying Guizhou, while Luo Bingzhang sent Liu Yuezhao to secure the north and protect Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 後專倚席寶田，戡定苗疆。

translations.literal: Later they relied exclusively on Xi Baotian to suppress and settle the Miao frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Later the work fell chiefly to Xi Baotian, who settled the Miao frontier.

sentences.zh: 自周達武以川兵、川餉濟黔之不及，曾璧光賴之以竟全功。

translations.literal: From the time Zhou Dawu used Sichuan troops and Sichuan funds to supply what Guizhou lacked, Ceng Biguang relied on this to complete the full achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Dawu brought Sichuan men and money to fill Guizhou's gaps, Ceng Biguang leaned on that partnership to finish the task.

sentences.zh: 蓋閱二十年而後大定。

translations.literal: In all it took more than twenty years before there was great pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Only after more than twenty years was the province truly at peace.

sentences.zh: 古云：「蠻夷之人，先叛後服。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Among barbarian peoples, they rebel first and submit afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Barbarian peoples rebel first and submit afterward.

sentences.zh: 」蓋以地勢使然。

translations.literal: "This is because terrain makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: "—and terrain makes it so.

sentences.zh: 然使若韓超者早膺疆寄，其延禍或不致如是之甚。

translations.literal: Yet if one like Han Chao had early borne a frontier charge, the prolongation of disaster might not have reached such severity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet had a man like Han Chao been given frontier command early, the catastrophe might never have grown so grave.

sentences.zh: 弭亂之道，在得其人，用人之道，必盡其才，固古今不爽者爾。

translations.literal: The way to quell disorder lies in getting the right man; the way to employ men must fully use their talents—this is what has never failed in ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification depends on the right man; employment must use talent to the full—a truth that has never changed in any age.
